_notes.authority: This whitelist is a DECLARATION, not a mute button. Every entry names a change, a count, a reason and the commit that made it legitimate. An undeclared change fails; a declared change that does not occur ALSO fails, because a stale entry is a hole nobody closed. Counts are per page/width comparison.
_notes.widths: Each page is loaded at both widths and fingerprinted separately. The site is responsive by CSS, so both widths should yield IDENTICAL markup -- if a page's DOM turns out to be width-dependent it is reported as a width anomaly, because a DOM-integrity result for such a page is per-width rather than general.
_notes.volatile: Two URL segments are normalized before comparison and nothing else: the ?v= content-hash cache stamp (P-A -- it changes whenever styles.css or a js/ file changes, which is exactly what a restyle does) and the hash segment of /fonts/<name>.<hash>.woff2 (the family name is KEPT, so substituting a different typeface still fails). Whether the bytes behind a font name are the right typeface is the fonts suite's question; it asserts computed faces against a real browser. Every other attribute compares raw.
_notes.text: Text is whitespace-normalized (rendering collapses whitespace anyway) and otherwise compared EXACTLY. A reworded sentence, a changed price or a dropped word is a failure. That is the instrument's purpose, not a limitation of it.
_notes.specificity: Every entry's "contains" must identify the node, not a family of nodes: the run refuses to start if an entry matches more nodes in the relevant build than it declares. A count is a budget, not an identity -- an entry held in check by its count alone consumes the first n matching changes rather than the ones it was written for, and starts absorbing a different node the moment the intended one stops changing. This is why the two Google preconnects are two entries keyed on their exact hrefs rather than one entry matching the word "preconnect" (which also matches the Cloudinary hint that must survive), and why the font preloads key on as="font" rather than "preload" (which also matches the hero image preload).
_notes.wp1b: WP-1b's full certification map, range-scoped to 198c0bb..c208508 (the batch commits vs their parent). Six reveal-class renames, six further class renames, six class REMOVALS (to:null -- the rhythm utilities and the cut warm-glow), two delete-subtree entries for the hero-intro hold, an added/removed pair for the five inline image radii, and a kind:code pair for booking-ops.html's reconciled --color-bg. Every count is measured against the real builds, not budgeted: the earlier note here recorded that the residual was wider than the four declared change classes and refused to widen the map to go green. This map is that residual ENUMERATED, which is the opposite move -- each line names one change, its reason and its commit, and the run reports what each consumed.
_notes.staleness: These four entries are the WP-1a declaration (commit 1877955 vs its parent) and they are the FIXTURE DATA for scripts/dom-integrity.test.mjs -- A1, A3, W8 and two mutation-battery properties (D-m6, D-m7) lose their coverage entirely without them. WP-1b tried removing them as stale and the suite caught it, which is the fixture-wins rule working. Consequence, stated so nobody rediscovers it as a bug: run this instrument against any baseline at or after 1877955 and all four report STALE WHITELIST, because the changes they declare are present on BOTH sides of that comparison. The entries are not wrong and the staleness check is not wrong -- the whitelist is per-COMPARISON while the file is per-repo, and the `commit` field records which comparison an entry belongs to without anything reading it. Resolving that is a harness change, not a batch change; flagged, not attempted here.
_notes.scope: Every entry declares the comparison it belongs to as "range": "<baselineSha>..<candidateSha>". The file is per-repo but each entry describes ONE batch's change, so without a scope an old batch's declarations sit here forever, reading stale against every later baseline while still being load-bearing. Out-of-scope entries are INERT for a run -- reported so they can be pruned, never consuming a diff they were not written for.
_notes.renameMap: An "op": "rename" entry declares an old->new CLASS TOKEN pair, applied to the BASELINE's vocabulary before anything is compared. Whole tokens only, never substrings, so renaming `fade-in` cannot touch `fade-in-late`. Everything the map does not explain survives into the comparison and still fails: a rename plus a smuggled extra class fails naming the smuggled token. A rename whose `from` never appears is flagged stale, so dead declarations cannot accumulate. A "to" of null declares that the token was REMOVED rather than renamed: the element survives and one of its class tokens goes, which no node entry can express. Same strictness -- an undeclared removal on the same node still fails.
_notes.deleteSubtree: A "delete-subtree" entry names a deleted node by tag + ancestry path + a HASH of its own serialized content, and consumes the whole run of removed tokens or nothing. It exists for attribute-less nodes, where the only substrings a `contains` entry could use are exactly the lazy kind the specificity check rejects. The hash cannot be written from memory -- it is measured from the baseline build -- and an entry whose hash matches nothing there is reported before any verdict rests on it. A nested subtree is ONE entry, not one per element.
_notes.kind: A removed/added entry names an ELEMENT unless it declares kind:"code" or kind:"text", in which case `contains` is matched against the token's TEXT. Without it an edit to an inline <style> body is undeclarable by construction, which is how booking-ops.html's :root reconciliation had no way to be certified. Kind is part of the entry's identity: a code entry cannot consume an element change even when its substring appears in an attribute.
